title: Text pair: The 7:12 and Letter on the Railway
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 53 (Text pair 'The 7:12' and 'Letter on the Railway' (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 53: Perspective: how a writer's viewpoint shapes a text. Teacher-written for TGA. Read, then answer under time.

passage.title: Text One: The 7:12
paras: Every weekday I spend fifty minutes on the 7:12. Most people treat it as dead time: phones, headphones, eyes shut. I used to. Then, one grey March, the signal failed for an hour outside a village I had passed five hundred times and never seen. A woman across the aisle offered me half her orange. A student read us the funny bits of his textbook. By the time the train moved, the carriage was a small, temporary town. It has never happened again. But now I look up from my phone, just in case.

passage.title: Text Two: Letter on the Railway
paras: Dear Mother, The railway has reached our town at last, and with it a noise I am not sure we shall ever grow used to. On Tuesday the first engine came in, breathing fire and steam like a creature from one of Father's old books. Half the town ran to the station; the other half ran away from it. The baker's horse broke its rope and was found two fields off, eating Mr Hale's cabbages. I confess I stood very near the platform's edge, and when the great wheels stopped I felt my heart had been running all the way from London with it.

questions.q: Write each writer's attitude in five words
questions.a: Letter: amazed, slightly frightened, delighted. Column: bored, then moved, hopeful.

questions.q: Find one detail shaped by each writer's time
questions.a: Letter: the horse breaking its rope; Column: phones and headphones.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write two comparative paragraphs on the writers' perspectives on train travel. Starter: 'Both writers..., but...'
questions.a: Two paragraphs comparing viewpoint, attitude and method with evidence from both texts and comparative connectives.

questions.q: Stretch: which perspective do you share? Explain with reference to both texts

options: The letter is old and the column is new.
The letter-writer is amazed by a new machine, whereas the columnist rediscovers wonder in an old routine.
questions.a: B) The letter-writer is amazed by a new machine, whereas the columnist rediscovers wonder in an old routine.. It compares viewpoint and attitude, not just topic or date.
B) the position a writer writes from
options: the position a writer writes from

questions.q: Answer the ponder: how can two writers make us feel so differently?
questions.a: Their position and time shape what they notice and how they say it.
